decision_conditions: The development to which this permission relates must be begun not later than the expiration of three years beginning with the date of the decision notice. Reason: To comply with the provisions of S.51 of the Planning & Compulsory Purchase Act 2004.

The development hereby permitted shall be carried out in accordance with the following approved plans:Location PlanProposed Block Plan received 11 February 2026Proposed Floor Plan Received 6 February 2026 Proposed Elevations Received 6 February 2026 Conservatory Proposed Plan Received 6 February 2026Conservatory Proposed Roof Plan Received 6 February 2026Conservatory Proposed Elevations 6 February 2026Reason: For the avoidance of doubt and in the interests of proper planning

All new external works to the existing pavilion shall use materials that closely match the colour, texture, and appearance of the existing building. The conservatory shall be constructed in accordance with the materials specified on the approved plans.Reason: To safeguard the visual appearance of the building and the character of the surrounding area

Notwithstanding the provisions of the Town and Country Planning (General Permitted Development) (England) Order 2015 (as amended) or any subsequent re-enactment, the premises shall only be used as a cafe open to members of the public and for no other purpose, including any other purpose within Class E of the Town and Country Planning (Use Classes) Order 1987 (as amended), unless otherwise agreed in writing by the Local Planning Authority.Reason: To ensure the café remains compatible with the park setting, does not result in unacceptable intensification, and prevents uses that could generate higher traffic, noise, or disturbance.

The café hereby permitted shall not be open to customers outside the hours of 08:00 to 22:00 on any day. The premises shall be closed on Christmas Day and Boxing Day, unless otherwise agreed in writing by the Local Planning Authority.Reason: To ensure the use operates in a manner appropriate to its park setting and to safeguard the amenity of the surrounding area.

Notwithstanding the details set out in the submitted Preliminary Drainage Strategy (Drawings A2071-1500 1503 P3, and A2071-1504 P1), prior to the commencement of any construction work, details of the Sustainable Drainage Strategy shall be submitted to and approved in writing by the Local Planning Authority and must conform with any Landscaping Strategy. The details shall include:Results of infiltration testing to determine the applicability of full and partial infiltration. If infiltration is not deemed acceptable through infiltration testing an appropriate attenuation feature must be provided in line with the London Plan Drainage Hierarchy Final sizes, storage volumes, invert levels, cross-sections and specifications of all SuDS measures including rain gardens, permeable paving, and soakaways Management Plan for future maintenanceReason: To ensure the sustainable management of water, minimise flood risk, minimise discharge of surface water outside of the curtilage of the property and ensure that the drainage system will remain functional throughout the lifetime of the development in accordance with Policy CP28 of the Core Strategy, DMD 61, and the London Plan and the NPPF

Prior to the first use of the cafe, a Fire Safety Strategy shall be submitted to and approved in writing by the Local Planning Authority. The strategy shall demonstrate how the development will achieve the highest standards of fire safety in accordance with Policy D12A of the London Plan, including details of:(a) evacuation arrangements and means of escape;(b) access and facilities for the fire service; and(c) measures to minimise the risk and spread of fire associated with the café use.The café shall thereafter be operated in accordance with the approved strategy.Reason: to ensure compliance with Policy D12 of the London Plan 2021

Prior to the commencement of the development hereby approved (including demolition and all preparatory work), a tree survey and a scheme for the protection of all retained trees compliant with BS 5837:2012 shall be submitted to and approved in writing by the Local Planning Authority. The scheme will comprise a detailed Arboricultural Method Statement (AMS) report supplemented by Tree Protection Plan(s) (TPP). The plan(s) shall be of legible scale and clearly show the layout (as agreed), all relevant existing site features that form a consideration within the protection scheme, and the location/extent of all appropriate protection measures.Specific matters to be addressed within the AMS and TPPs will include:a) location and installation of all utililty services/drainage, avoiding the Root Protection Areas(RPA) of all retained trees and being compatible with any proposed planting(RPA as defined within BS 5837:2012);b) methods of demolition of existing structures within or directly adjacent to RPAs and the removal of existing hard standing and kerb edging within or directly adjacent to RPAs;c) details of any construction that necessitate level changes within RPAs;d) details of all foundation design, and installation methodology within or adjacent to RPAs;e) a full specification for the construction of all roads, paths, parking areas and driveways (including alterations to the existing layout of internal roads and hard standing) within RPAs. Where a no-dig sub-base is specified (e.g. cellular confinement system) a specification shall be provided (including a diagrammatical cross-section of the product in-situ) and extent of areas where this would be implemented illustrated within the TPP;f) detailed levels and cross-sections to show that the raised levels of surfacing where the installation of no-dig surfacing within RPAs is proposed, demonstrating that the raised areas can be effectively integrated with prevailing levels where they meet with adjacent surfacing or building damp proof courses;g) a full specification for the installation of boundary treatments within or directly adjacent to RPAs;h) a specification for protective fencing and, if necessary, ground protection, to safeguard all treesduring both demolition and construction phases. The Tree Protection Plan(s) shall clearly indicatethe alignment of the fencing and extent of ground protection;i) a specification for scaffolding and ground protection in Construction Exclusion Zones (where necessary);j) details of site access, temporary parking, on site welfare facilities, loading, unloading and storage of equipment, materials, fuels and waste as well concrete mixing and siting of fires;The development thereafter shall be implemented in strict accordance with the approved details.Reason: Required prior to commencement of development to satisfy the Local Planning Authority that the trees to be retained will not be damaged during demolition or construction and to protect and enhance the appearance and character of the site and locality, in accordance with Policy DM D80 (Trees on Development Sites) and pursuant to section 197 of the Town and Country Planning Act 1990.

Prior to the commencement of the café use, a Waste and Recycling Management Strategy shall be submitted to and approved in writing by the Local Planning Authority. The strategy shall include:o	Details of refuse and recycling storage locations;o	Capacity of bins;o	Collection arrangements and frequency;o	Measures to prevent littering within the park;o	Measures to prevent odour and vermin;o	Details of how waste will be transported to and from the site.The approved strategy shall be implemented prior to first use of the café and thereafter retained and operated in accordance with the approved details.Reason: To ensure appropriate waste management arrangements in the interests of visual amenity, public health, and the character of the park setting.

Prior to the commencement of the use and unless otherwise agreed in writing, cycle parking should be provided in compliance with the following criteria: a)Provision of a minimum of 2 long stay cycle parking spaces and 3 short stay spaces (long and short stay must be separate) b)in an accessible location: the access route to the long stay store should be a minimum of 1.2m wide to enable the bike to enter the store, should be step free and involve no more than 2 doors or gates (excluding the store door) which must also have a minimum opening of 1.2m Short stay must also have a clear 1.2m level access route and must be in a well over looked area. c)Long stay spaces must be secured: with a British Standard mortice lock or access fobd)long stay spaces must be fully enclosed with 4 walls and a roof. Reason: The council's Climate Action and Transport Policies seek to increase the use of active and sustainable transport modes. this means that the access to bicycle parking should be easy and secure to remove potential barriers to cycling.

Prior to the installation of any means of enclosure, the details of the enclosure shall be submitted to and approved in writing by the Local Planning Authority. The facilities shall be provided in accordance with the approved details before the development is occupied or use commences.  Reason: In the interests of highway safety and accessibility.

No external lighting shall be installed on the building or elsewhere within the site unless details have first been submitted to and approved in writing by the Local Planning Authority. The details shall include the location, design, luminance levels and direction of lighting. The lighting shall thereafter be installed and operated only in accordance with the approved details.Reason: To safeguard the character and appearance of the park, the setting of nearby heritage assets, and to ensure that lighting does not result in unnecessary light spill that could harm biodiversity

No externally audible amplified music or sound shall be played within the outdoor areas of the site at any time.Reason: To safeguard the amenity of park users and nearby residents and to preserve the tranquil character of the park environment.
